The sparse engine can estimate its memory needs before a solve, enforce a
per-model memory budget, and retain additional solve diagnostics when asked.
The examples below use the small generated fixture shared with the other
vignettes.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)
helperPath = if (file.exists("helpers.R")) {
  "helpers.R"
} else {
  file.path("vignettes", "helpers.R")
}
source(helperPath, local = knitr::knit_global())
fixture = makeFirstSimulationFixture()
model = GEModelR::GEModel$new()
model$loadTablo(fixture$tabloPath)
model$setClosure("tax")
model$loadData(fixture$inputData, engine = "sparse")
model$setShocks(setNames(4, 'tax["south"]'))
```

## Estimate before solving

`estimateMemory()` reports an estimate for the selected engine and whether
post-simulation work is included. Use it as planning information for the
model and runtime you are about to execute:

```{r estimate-memory}
memoryEstimate = model$estimateMemory(engine = "sparse", postsim = FALSE)
print(memoryEstimate)
```

The public estimate describes generic sparse storage. During `solveModel()`,
the selected structured backend additionally accounts for its partition:
dense regional/global matrices and factors, simultaneously live copies,
coupling transfers, local factor fill, Arnoldi vectors and worker scratch.
The budget guard uses this fuller estimate before assembly. Counts from the
original partition can overestimate storage later removed by elimination.
Factor fill and allocator overhead remain estimates; this is not a hard cap
on process RSS. Detailed solve diagnostics retain the component estimates.

## Set a memory budget

`setMemoryBudget(bytes)` stores an instance-level sparse budget. A solve fails
during preflight if its estimate exceeds the available budget. The example
sets a one-gibibyte budget, ample for this tiny fixture. The `memory_budget`
argument to `solveModel()` can instead set or override the budget for one
solve.

```{r set-memory-budget}
model$setMemoryBudget(1024^3)
```

## Request compact output and detailed diagnostics

Compact output avoids materializing the full compatibility output structure.
By default, `diagnostics = FALSE` stores the compact stable outcome envelope.
Set `diagnostics = TRUE` when you also need residual history, timings,
allocation and capability evidence, detailed cleanup, and memory estimates.

```{r solve-with-diagnostics}
model$solveModel(
  iter = 1,
  steps = 1,
  engine = "sparse",
  backend = "Matrix",
  postsim = FALSE,
  output = "compact",
  variables = "q",
  diagnostics = TRUE
)
model$compactOutput
```

The top-level diagnostics fields include the requested runtime and backend,
the implementation selected, and the solve status:

```{r inspect-diagnostics}
model$lastDiagnostics[c(
  "schema_version", "engine", "requested_backend", "implementation", "status"
)]
```

For the stable field list and failure statuses, see the
```{r package-help-link, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
# pkgdown sets IN_PKGDOWN while rendering articles.
helpPage = if (identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")) {
  "../reference/GEModelR-package.html"
} else {
  "../html/GEModelR-package.html"
}
cat(sprintf("[GEModelR package help](%s)", helpPage))
```
Diagnostics add evidence to the record; they do not change which backend was
requested or permit fallback.

Every accepted sparse solution passes the full-system check
$\lVert A x-b\rVert_2 / \max(1,\lVert b\rVert_2)$ at the documented
residual tolerance. Scaled arithmetic forms this ratio without overflowing
the denominator. Invalid products or non-finite residual entries fail before
state is committed. An absolute L2 diagnostic can be infinite when its exact
value exceeds the double range; acceptance still requires a finite scaled
relative residual. Small RHS vectors retain the existing absolute-tolerance
semantics.

The C++ backend carries only structural metadata between solves. Its keys
include index/closure layout, sparse pattern, grouping and batching settings.
Numeric factors and regional transfers belong to one solve and are rebuilt
after coefficient changes. Prepared sparse factors own validated snapshots
and reusable scratch; cleanup releases native handles before results are
committed or a failure is returned. Matrix references needed for acceptance
are released before simulation updates.

With detailed diagnostics, `phase_allocations` reports nonnegative changes in
sampled R heap usage. Samples use full garbage collections and R's reported
MiB, including the platform-specific size of node cells. `peak_gc_bytes` is
the largest of those phase samples across the solve; the same samples are
reused for progress and final diagnostics. These rounded heap estimates do
not include all native allocations and are distinct from process peak RSS.
